scope: Proposition 4.14 (Pruned old graph) of the manuscript “A torsion-free counterexample to reduced Baum–Connes injectivity” (preprints/A-Torsion-Free-Counterexample-to-Reduced-Baum-Connes-Injectivity-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 285 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 df8d9301aa6d0306), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 37. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Given any ε > 0, the allowed parameters and the universal tables can be chosen so that the additional two deletions in this Section remove less than an ε fraction of each Ai and Bi. In the surviving induced old graph Xold: 1. the folded labeling, padded-prefix recovery of Lemma 2.4, and global word uniqueness of Proposition 2.6 remain valid; 2. a nonempty cyclically reduced closed path based at height i has length greater than .93mi; 3. every bicycle containing a vertex of height i has length at least 1.52mi; 4. every nonempty cyclically reduced closed path based at height i with length at most 6.04mi is not a law in the independent edge variables of H. The expansion conclusions for the undeleted incidences hold simultaneously, and the degrees remain fixed along the tower.
